plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the outline; a Master Services Agreement of this type almost always carries a limitation of liability article. Scan the full body for 'Limitation of Liability', consequential damages waivers and any cap tied to fees paid, checking mutuality and carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, willful misconduct).

Expect a vendor indemnity article in the operative text not surfaced in the outline. Look for third-party IP infringement indemnity running to AP, defence/control language, and any reciprocal or broader customer indemnity that should be narrowed.

Restrictive covenants on the customer are uncommon in an ad-tech MSA; nothing in the visible outline suggests one. Confirm by searching the body for 'compete', 'competing business' or 'restricted activities' before concluding the rule is inapplicable.

No exclusivity heading is visible. Check the services/scope and term provisions for 'exclusive', 'sole provider' or 'shall not engage any third party' language that would bind AP; flag only if AP's freedom to source elsewhere is curtailed.

MFN clauses are rare in vendor-form MSAs. Search fees/pricing text for 'most favoured/favored nation' or 'no less favourable terms'; an MFN running in AP's favour is welcome and should not be touched.

Non-solicit clauses commonly sit near confidentiality or general provisions. Verify duration (12 months preferred), that it is mutual, limited to employees engaged under the agreement, and carves out general advertising and unsolicited applicants.

The preamble defines 'Initial Term', so a Term and Termination article exists in the unexposed body. Check whether AP has termination for convenience on notice without penalty and whether Kubient holds a symmetric right that would let it exit mid-term.

'Initial Term' is a defined term, so renewal mechanics should follow in the term article. Confirm the non-renewal notice window (30 days preferred, 60 acceptable) and whether renewal pricing is capped or uncapped.

Expect governing law and venue in the general/miscellaneous provisions. Confirm the chosen law is New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign-seated arbitration.

Assignment sits in miscellaneous provisions in nearly all MSAs. Check that AP may assign to affiliates and to a successor in a merger or asset sale without consent, and that a change of control of AP does not trigger Kubient termination.

Look for an intellectual property / ownership article and any data-use or aggregated-analytics language. Confirm AP retains ownership of its content and data and that deliverables paid for are assigned to AP, with no grant of AP IP to Kubient beyond a service-delivery licence.

Check the grant clause in the services/licence provisions for scope: it should extend to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf and must not be revocable at Kubient's discretion during the term.

Audit or records-inspection language often appears near fees/payment or compliance. Confirm any audit of AP is no more than annual, on reasonable prior notice, during business hours, off-site where feasible and at Kubient's cost absent a material discrepancy; note that AP-side audit rights over Kubient reporting are beneficial and should not be flagged.
Search fees/termination text for 'liquidated damages', 'early termination fee' or 'penalty' payable by AP. Service credits or SLA credits running to AP are favourable and must not be redlined.

Expect a representations and warranties article, possibly followed by a broad disclaimer. Check for a services performance warranty of meaningful duration with re-performance or refund as remedy, and whether an 'AS IS' disclaimer negates it.

Insurance is frequently omitted from vendor-form ad-tech MSAs. Search for 'insurance', 'coverage' or certificate-of-insurance language; if none exists and Kubient touches AP data, treat the rule as missing and request standard commercial, cyber/tech E&O and workers' comp coverage.
Check the fees/payment provisions and any order form or exhibit for minimum spend, take-or-pay, or committed volume language binding AP; if present, confirm there is a termination or true-down exit.

Look at the effect-of-termination provisions for data return/deletion and transition assistance. Vendor forms often provide only for deletion of confidential information; if there is no right for AP to retrieve its data and receive migration help, treat as missing.
